images.title: Base 3 landmarks
images.purpose: Shows that the landmarks of a base 3 system are 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, each 3 times the one before.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Five circles growing in size from left to right with an arrow between each pair and a heading above.
images.exact_structure: Top centre heading: base 3. Below it, exactly 5 teal (#0072B2) circles in a row, each larger than the one on its left, with its value in white: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81. Between each pair, one amber (#E69F00) arrow labelled × 3, exactly 4 arrows. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In base n the landmarks start at 1 and multiply by n each time.
images.description: Shows that the landmarks of a base 3 system are 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, each 3 times the one before.

image_decisions.why: The definition of base n is a rule for making landmarks; a growing chain shows the rule with base 3.
